notes: Hard (total 18). A staged exploit chain, each stage gated by the previous one (dependent_stages=3): (1) craft a working SQL-injection payload to authenticate as a target account; (2) craft an exact byte-level overflow payload that flips an adjacent gating field inside a fixed struct to a specific magic constant, unlocking the protected branch that prints the lone deployment secret; (3) run the Flask service's authorize_deployment() with that secret so its body actually executes and writes a side-effect grants file; (4) harden /app/app.py so any unknown /lookup/<id> returns HTTP 404 with a JSON error body and no HTML or stack trace. Reasoning is threefold (reasoning_depth=3): deriving the SQL tautology (easy) and C struct offset/magic-constant layout so the 20-byte payload lands exactly on the gate (quantitative=3, exact bytes and exact value), and the 404 hardening. The overflow symptom is ambiguous: an underrun or wrong-length payload prints only locked, so the agent must infer the buffer/field layout from source alone (debugging_ambiguity=2). generalization=3 because the verifier replays the payload against several target accounts, re-runs the deployment check against a fresh hash verification, and hits a battery of malformed/special-case not-found IDs (adversarial=2, ids with spaces, dots, SQL-ish text, long strings) that must not 500. Hard floors: C-1f4f846b requires actually running the app to emit the side-effect file (hard); C-1aefef55 and C-9c9c34df are medium. Correctness is numeric/exact (magic constant 0x9E1C, sha256 digest match, exact 20-byte payload).
